case_title: Antibiotic-associated SIADH with severe hypotonic hyponatremia and generalized tonic-clonic seizures
disease_label_per_paper: SIADH complicated by generalized tonic-clonic seizures after a course of antibiotics
rankable_evidence_window: Pre-treatment symptoms, antibiotic exposure, seizure presentation, volume context, and first blood/urine chemistry are rankable. Hypertonic saline response, sodium normalization, MHRA reporting, and culprit-drug attribution are record-only.

risk_context.source_text_value: Completed a 3-day course of nitrofurantoin in the 10 days before presentation.
Completed a 5-day course of cephalexin after nitrofurantoin.
Increased fluid intake by 50% thinking she could flush out the infection.

presentation_summary: A 48-year-old woman presented with one week of nausea, dizziness, fatigue, and listlessness after antibiotic treatment for urinary symptoms.
While waiting in the emergency department she had two self-limiting generalized tonic-clonic seizures with tongue biting and minor head trauma.
Initial labs showed severe hypotonic hyponatremia: serum sodium 114 mmol/L and serum osmolality 240 mOsm/kg.
Spot urine remained inappropriately concentrated with urine osmolality 264 mOsm/kg and urine sodium 76 mmol/L.
She was treated with hypertonic saline and fluid restriction; sodium correction and final drug attribution are kept non-ranking.

clinical_course_events.event: 0.9% sodium chloride was initially started in the immediate post-ictal period.
clinical_course_events.source_text_value: A bag of 0.9% sodium chloride was initially set up in the immediate post-ictal period.

clinical_course_events.event: Levetiracetam 2 g IV was administered to prevent further seizures.
clinical_course_events.source_text_value: The patient was given an intravenous bolus of levetiracetam 2 g.

clinical_course_events.event: After severe hyponatremia was recognized, she received 5% hypertonic saline 100 mL over one hour and fluid restriction.
clinical_course_events.source_text_value: The infusion was changed to a bolus of 5% hypertonic saline at 100 mL over one hour, and she was advised to restrict fluid intake to less than 1.5 liters a day.

actual_treatment: 5% hypertonic saline 100 mL over one hour

outcome.source_text_value: Serum sodium normalized to 134 mmol/L by the day after admission, she was discharged, and follow-up electrolytes were normal.

quality_warnings: This case combines drug-induced SIADH and severe neurologic presentation; the post-treatment sodium rise is record-only.
Culprit attribution to nitrofurantoin versus cephalexin is not used for ranking.
